cf.title: pg_combinebackup: Don't point only to pg_checksums for mixed checksum states

input.subject: Offline data checksum changes can cause incorrect checksum state on standbys

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The patch rewords one pg_combinebackup hint and one documentation paragraph and leaves the refusal as it is. Confidence is low because the material shows neither the new hint wording nor the new docs text, and nobody has replied to message #44.

brief.title: pg_combinebackup: drop pg_checksums from the mixed checksum state hint
brief.problem: pg_combinebackup refuses a backup chain whose backups have different data checksum states. Its hint then says the state was changed "with pg_checksums", even when the user enabled checksums online with pg_enable_data_checksums(). The same wrong hint appears when the full backup was taken while checksums were still being enabled (version 3 in pg_control).
brief.proposed_design: The patch removes "with pg_checksums" from the hint. It also rewrites the Limitations paragraph of the pg_combinebackup docs to cover offline enabling, online enabling and the in-progress state. The refusal itself stays as it is.
user_visible_surface: Changed hint text for the pg_combinebackup error "only some backups have checksums enabled".
Changed Limitations paragraph in the pg_combinebackup documentation.
author_claims: The current hint names a tool that the user may never have run.
pg_combinebackup tests and test_checksums 024_combinebackup_mixed (PG_TEST_EXTRA=checksum) pass, and the docs validate.
After an online enable, the refusal is stricter than needed, because the worker WAL-logs every page and the next incremental backup sends every relation file in full.
pg_combinebackup cannot tell an online enable from an offline one using the control files, so refusing both is the safe choice.
brief.thread_state: The 44-message thread produced the refusal in pg_combinebackup, which was pushed to master in September and not yet backpatched at that time. Message #44 posts this follow-up patch and nobody has replied to it.
unclear: The material gives neither the new hint wording nor the new docs text, and shows no commit message for this patch.
The CommitFest entry targets version 20, but the refusal comes from the v19 open-item work, and the patch does not say whether it should go into 19.
The author does not say whether the docs should mention that the refusal is stricter than needed after an online enable.

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows pg_combinebackup and the v19 data checksums work would own it. Committers took part earlier in the thread, but none has replied to message #44.
committability.liability: One hint string, with its translations, and one documentation paragraph. The owner also decides whether to backpatch to 19, where the refusal may land.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the author posted the patch in message #44 and created the CommitFest entry, and no review has arrived yet.

priority.reason: Only users who change the checksum state inside an incremental backup chain see this hint, but for them the current text names a tool they may never have run. The patch changes one string and one docs paragraph, so review is short.

precedents_retrieved.title: teach pg_combinebackup to detect deleted files where possible
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_combinebackup would look up every file of the final input backup in its backup_manifest and warn about manifest entries that are missing on disk. This catches files deleted from the most recent backup, without reading or checksumming file contents.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas withdrew the patch because no one besides David Steele asked for it. He had mixed feelings about it: the check covers only missing files in the final backup and may give users a false sense of security, and pg_verifybackup already does full verification. Amul Sul reviewed the code but took no position on the idea.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Nobody else has responded. Hence, I'm withdrawing this patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enabling data checksums in an online cluster
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal turns the data checksum flag into a three-state value (off/inprogress/on) and adds pg_enable_data_checksums() and pg_disable_data_checksums(), so that checksums can be turned on in a running cluster. A background launcher starts a worker in each database that rewrites every page with a valid checksum, WAL-logged with full-page writes, and switches the state to "on" when all databases are done; an offline pg_verify_checksums tool is also included.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The deciding factor was inactivity: in January 2019 the commitfest entry was proposed for Returned With Feedback because the patch had not been developed for several months, and the author agreed, citing circumstances outside his control. Earlier visible messages show unresolved points: buildfarm/isolation test failures on platforms without atomics in April 2018, a July 2018 discussion about whether a restart should be required during enabling, and a September 2018 question about how disabling checksums interacts with tools that verify checksums online. The visible messages do not show that any of these was itself the reason the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Given that this patch has not been developed in a few months, I don't
see why this has an active 2019-01 CF entry?

precedents_retrieved.title: SLRU data page checksums
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add checksums to SLRU pages (clog, multixact, commit timestamps, subtrans and similar), stored in the last two bytes of each page, computed on write and verified on read when data checksums are enabled. A new GUC, ignore_slru_checksum_failure, would turn verification failures into warnings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The shown messages do not include a closing decision, but they record unresolved problems. Thomas Munro pointed out that SLRU pages have no full-page-write protection, so a torn page after power loss would fail checksum verification and could stop recovery, and whole-page checksums are incompatible with the incremental redo of SLRU pages. Earlier, Alexander Korotkov noted that pg_upgrade support for the changed usable page size was missing. Andres Freund backed a different approach, adding regular page headers to SLRU blocks, which Shawn Debnath said he was working on.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: With your patch, a torn SLRU page can cause recovery to fail.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow pg_verify_checksums to specify a database to scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add options to pg_verify_checksums to limit checksum verification to one database, given by OID with -d/--dboid, or to shared relations only with -g/--global-only. This follows a discussion that the existing -r RELFILENODE option had no way to say which database it referred to.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO's review asked for several changes: TAP tests (the command had none), stricter parsing of the OID argument, handling of -d and -g given together (that combination succeeded while checking nothing), and documentation fixes. Masahiko Sawada suggested allowing several database OIDs. The thread ends with these review comments and shows no revised patch before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: When the command is started with both "-d 1 -g", it succeeds by checking nothing, which is quite misleading. Probably it should complain that these options are mutually exclusive, or it should check both under -g AND -d 1?

precedents_retrieved.title: invalid data in file backup_label problem on windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, a backup_label file written with CRLF line endings makes recovery fail with "invalid data in file backup_label", because the parser expects '\n' after each line. The patch opened backup_label and tablespace_map in text mode when reading them, so the server would accept CRLF line endings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread switched from changing the server to a documentation fix. The fix tells users to write backup_label byte for byte, in binary mode. David Steele's documentation patch was committed and backpatched as 6fb66c26, and the author agreed to write the file in binary mode, so the entry was withdrawn. The messages that argued against the server change are in the part of the thread not shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It's not hurtful anywhere, there's really no reason ever to open it in text mode.

precedents_retrieved.title: Checksums for slru files
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alexander Korotkov, Thomas Munro, Andres Freund
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a checksum in the last 2 bytes of every SLRU page, computed on write and verified on read when data checksums are enabled. A new GUC, ignore_slru_checksum_failure, turns verification failures into warnings, like ignore_checksum_failure does for relations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for pg_upgrade support that moves existing SLRU data to the smaller usable page size, plus tests for it. They also found SLRU per-page macros the patch did not update. The author did not reply, and the patch was returned with feedback after a commitfest in Waiting on Author with no progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch is in the 2018-03 CF, but I don't see any progress since the
last comments. As it has been Waiting on author since the last CF, I
think we should mark this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: An attempt to avoid locally-committed-but-not-replicated-to-standby-transactions in synchronous replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, synchronous_replication_naptime_before_cancel, that makes a backend keep waiting for the sync standby ack for a set time before it handles a query cancel or proc die. A second part, not yet coded, would make the primary wait for sync standbys to catch up after a crash restart before it serves the locally committed transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the patch received no update for six months and no longer applied. The design was still open at the last author message. The author could not reliably detect, at restart, that a backend died while waiting for the sync replication ack, and the alternative of always waiting could keep the primary down. Earlier, Laurenz Albe objected that the approach still left some cases of transactions committed locally but not on the standby.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since there hasn't been any updates for the past six months, and the patch
hasn't applied for a few months, I am marking this returned with feedback for
now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add GiST support for mixed-width integer operators
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds pg_amop entries to btree_gist's opfamilies so that GiST indexes can serve cross-type comparisons (all five btree operators across int2/int4/int8, later also float4/float8 and date/timestamp/timestamptz), placing each mixed-width operator in the opfamily of the wider type. The goal was to let queries such as id = 5 on a bigint column use the GiST index without an explicit cast.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane pointed out that the patch only added catalog entries without changing the C consistent functions, which assume the comparison value has the opclass's own type; this gives wrong results when values are truncated, is a type violation even when it appears to work, and can crash on 32-bit machines where int8 is pass-by-reference. Timestamp-vs-timestamptz comparisons would also need a timezone conversion the code does not perform. He suggested that a working design would need new strategy numbers encoding the RHS type and substantial new cross-type code in the consistent functions; no revised patch appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Perhaps I'm missing something, but how can this possibly work without
any changes to the C code?

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no row about this or a similar idea. The thread does not point to an earlier attempt to change this hint, and the patch only rewords a hint and a docs paragraph, so no earlier rejection reason applies.

From the standards and compatibility angle, the patch changes only the wording of one hint and one documentation paragraph. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or dump format, and the behaviour stays the same. A shorter hint without the tool name still tells the user what to do. The new hint and docs text are not in the material, so their wording could not be checked. Whether the change goes into 19 together with the refusal is a backpatch question for the committer, not a compatibility risk.

The patch changes only a client-side hint string and a documentation paragraph. It adds no on-disk, WAL, control file, catalog, protocol or ABI change, and the refusal logic stays as it is, so this angle has nothing to object to.

The patch changes only a hint string and a documentation paragraph for pg_combinebackup, a client tool run by whoever already holds the backup files. Nothing changes who can do or see what, and the refusal itself stays as it is, so there is no security or privilege aspect to object to.

The patch changes one hint string and one docs paragraph and adds no code path, GUC, catalog or API, so it carries no ongoing maintenance or hot-path cost. Not checked: the new hint and docs wording, which the material does not show, and whether the change should go into 19 along with the refusal.

The patch only corrects a hint and a docs paragraph for a refusal added in this release cycle. No existing feature, extension or tool gives users a correct hint, and the patch adds no new mechanism, so this angle has nothing to object to.

No demand objection applies. The patch fixes a hint that names pg_checksums when the user enabled checksums online with pg_enable_data_checksums(), and the reproducer in message #44 shows this. Every user of the new online-enable path who meets the refusal sees that hint, and the change adds no new surface, cost or maintenance burden.
